facts.statement: The genus Heteroptychodus was described by Yabe and Obata in 1930.
Three species are known within the genus: Heteroptychodus chuvalovi, Heteroptychodus kokutensis, and Heteroptychodus steinmanni.
Heteroptychodus was an extinct hybodont shark that lived in Asia during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Heteroptychodus is an extinct genus of hybodont that lived in Asia during the Early Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The animal possessed low, rounded teeth designed for crushing hard objects, which were covered in ridges.
facts.quote: It had low, rounded durophagous teeth that are covered in ridges.

facts.statement: Fossils of this genus have been found in Japan, Mongolia, Malaysia, Thailand, Southern China, and possibly Kyrgyzstan.
facts.quote: Species have been reported from Japan, Mongolia, Malaysia, Thailand, Southern China, and possibly Kyrgyzstan.

facts.statement: Fossils of Heteroptychodus have been recovered from freshwater environments.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in freshwater environments.

facts.statement: Heteroptychodus belongs to the subfamily Hybodontinae.
The genus is classified within the family Hybodontidae.
Heteroptychodus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish.
The genus lived from the Tithonian to the Albian stages, between 149.2 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Albian (149.2 to 100.5 million years ago)
